newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah weakens on improved liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah weakens on improved liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the dollar in slow late trading on Wednesday on the back of increased liquidity in the money market, dealers said.
One Japanese bank dealer said liquidity was driving the market, shrugging off the healthy February trade surplus and moderate rise in April prices announced in the morning.
Desmond Supple, head of research for Asian currencies with BZW Barclays in Singapore, said the rupiah was not going to react on economic fundamentals for now.
"Focus is squarely on liquidity and political risks. I remain cautious on the rupiah," Supple said.
"But once the event risk of the (May 29 general) elections is out of the way, then the rupiah could begin to reflect some of the country's fundamentals," Supple said.
The trade surplus rose to $964.3 million in February from $575.4 million in January and inflation was 0.56 percent in April against a decline of 0.12 percent in March.
Economists said the figures were encouraging, but suggested the government needed further trade reforms to improve non-oil exports after flat growth in the last quarter of 1996.
Spot rupiah was at 2,429.50/29.75 at 0915 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,425.50/26.50.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,428.0/28.5 and 2,425.50/26.25, respectively.
Dealers said the dollar strengthened in the afternoon after overnight rates softened to 12.0 percent from 17.0 percent in the morning. Overnight swaps eased to 1.10/1.25 from 1.25/1.5.
But they said longer-term swaps were little changed.
One-month swaps were at 13.25/13.75, two at 26.50/27.00, three at 38.0/39.0 and six at 76.5/78.0 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,408/2,600 and the conversion band to 2,408/2,456 on Wednesday. The market will be closed on Thursday for a public holiday.
